coverage_notes:
WHAT I RECOVERED: The full on-field tier is complete and well-sourced — head coach Lloyd Carr plus all 9 full-time assistants (NCAA's limit at the time), each with a specific position title from the Wikipedia team-season page's "Coaching staff" table, cross-checked against U-M's own official year-by-year assistant-staff list (mgoblue.com) and the 1997 team photograph caption archived by the Bentley Historical Library. Beyond that I recovered strength & conditioning (Gittleson), the head trainer (Schmidt), equipment (Falk), video (Bromley), two graduate assistants (Goodwin, Draper), one student assistant (Elston), six student managers, and four additional back-row staff whose titles I could not determine.

SOURCE CONFLICT I RESOLVED: The Bentley Historical Library's 1997 page lists "Greg Mattison" among the assistant coaches. That is an error carried over from its 1996 page. Mattison left Michigan for Notre Dame in 1997 (he coached there 1997-2004); he does NOT appear in the 1997 team photograph on that same Bentley page, while Terry Malone does. U-M's official assistant-coaching-staffs list also shows Malone, not Mattison, for 1997. I have therefore excluded Mattison and included Malone. Anyone re-deriving this from Bentley's prose list alone will get a false positive.

TIERS I COULD NOT RECOVER:
- ANALYST and QUALITY CONTROL: zero rows. These were not staff categories that existed as formal titles in 1997 college football; Michigan had no such positions. Nothing omitted, nothing invented.
- OPERATIONS/PERSONNEL/RECRUITING: no dedicated director of football operations or recruiting-ops staffer is documented for 1997. Recruiting-coordinator duties were held by Bobby Morrison as part of his on-field job (Wikipedia infobox renders his 1997-2002 Michigan role as "ST/RC"), so he is categorized onfield, not ops. Michigan's first separately-titled Director of Football Operations appears in the record well after 1997.
- ADDITIONAL S&C STAFF: only Gittleson is documented. Any assistant strength coaches are unrecoverable.
- COMPLETE GA LIST: Michigan carried two graduate-assistant slots. Goodwin and Draper are each independently documented as GAs covering 1997, and Elston as a student assistant that season, but I cannot certify this is the exhaustive GA/student-assistant roster.
- ADDITIONAL MEDICAL/TRAINING STAFF: only Paul Schmidt is documented by title ("Trainer"). Michigan certainly carried more athletic trainers; Todd Jager, Kevin Lynch and Rick Clark (below) are plausible candidates but I found no source stating their roles, so I did not guess.

FOUR NAMED-BUT-UNTITLED STAFF: Todd Jager, Kevin Lynch, Rick Clark and Chris Kurpeikis appear in the back row of the official 1997 team photograph — the row reserved for coaches and support staff, and the same row containing Schmidt, Gittleson, Falk, Bromley, Draper, Goodwin and Elston. They are real, sourced staff members, but no source I found states their titles, so their role field says exactly that and they are categorized "other" rather than assigned a plausible-sounding job.

DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED: The team photo's 8th row (Eddie Davis, Eric Dean, Ethan Perkins, Bob Bland, Rick Brandt, Steve Connelly, Scott Loeffler, and others) mixes student managers with actual players — Scott Loeffler was the roster's #15 quarterback — so I could not safely treat that row as a staff list and did not enumerate it. Notably Bob Bland and Rick Brandt were Michigan's assistant equipment managers by 2008 and are plausibly the same in 1997, but no 1997-era source states this, so I left them out rather than pad.

SOURCE-AVAILABILITY LIMITS: Step 2 of the requested method failed — the Wayback Machine has NO archived staff directory or coaches page for Michigan's 1997-98 athletics site (umich.edu/~mgoblue/Football/97-98/); only game recaps, releases and player pages were captured. Step 3 also failed: the 1997 Michigan media guide is not available on the school site, archive.org, or issuu. Support-staff titles therefore come from later official U-M bios and news sources whose stated tenure spans demonstrably cover 1997 (e.g. Gittleson "26th season" in 2004, Bromley "33rd season" in 2022, Falk "since 1974"), anchored to 1997 presence by the team photograph. Note also that bentley.umich.edu returns HTTP 403 to automated fetches; I cite the Wayback capture, which serves identical text.

MID-SEASON CHANGES: none found. No arrivals or departures during the 1997 season are documented, so no midseason_note is set on any row; every person listed was on staff through the Jan. 1, 1998 Rose Bowl.
